description: Sync rows from the BigQuery tables you choose, one searchable document per row.
intro: The BigQuery connector reads the tables you select in one Google Cloud project. Each row becomes one document. Its text lists every non-empty column as a label and a value, and the document is grouped under its table.
You decide, table by table, how HydraDB finds new and changed rows: a timestamp column, BigQuery's change history, or a full read of the table on every sync.

connect.text: Set a primary key for every table you select. HydraDB updates a row's document by its key. If a table has no real unique key, different rows can be treated as the same document and replace each other.

connect.auth: BigQuery uses a Google Cloud service account. There is no sign-in flow: you paste credentials. Supply one complete set: a service-account key file, a service-account email with its private key, or an OAuth client id, client secret and refresh token.

credentials.name: credentials_json
credentials.text: The service account's JSON key file, pasted whole. This is the recommended option.

credentials.name: client_email
credentials.text: The service account's email. Use it together with `private_key` instead of the key file.

credentials.name: private_key
credentials.text: The service account's private key. Use it together with `client_email`.

credentials.name: client_id
credentials.text: An OAuth client id. Valid only together with `client_secret` and `refresh_token`.

credentials.name: client_secret
credentials.text: An OAuth client secret. Valid only together with `client_id` and `refresh_token`.

credentials.name: refresh_token
credentials.text: An OAuth refresh token you issued beforehand. It is required in the OAuth option, because a client id and secret alone cannot reach BigQuery.

connect.credentials_note: Each credential field is optional on its own, but one of the three options must be complete.

settings.name: project_id
settings.text: The Google Cloud project to read. Required unless the key file already names a project.

settings.name: location
settings.text: The BigQuery location to run query jobs in.

settings.name: datasets
settings.text: Limits discovery and sync to these datasets.

settings.name: replication_key
settings.text: A timestamp column to use as the sync cursor for every selected table that has it. A table's own setting overrides it.

settings.name: change_history
settings.text: `appends` or `changes`, used for tables that still have no cursor column. A table's own setting overrides it.

settings.name: detect_replication_from_partitioning
settings.text: Off by default. When on, column-partitioned tables sync incrementally on their partition column.

permissions.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/bigquery
permissions.text: scope, in the OAuth option. Google rejects query jobs under the read-only BigQuery scope.

steps.title: Create a service account
steps.text: In Google Cloud, create a service account. Give it the BigQuery Data Viewer and BigQuery Job User roles on the project, and download its JSON key.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the key as `credentials_json`. Add `project_id` only if the key file does not name a project. To narrow what discovery shows, list `datasets`.

steps.title: Select tables
steps.text: Discover lists the tables in the project, narrowed by `datasets` when you set it. Select the tables to sync. Each selected table becomes its own set of documents, one per row.

steps.title: Choose a sync mode for each table
steps.text: If the table has a timestamp column that changes on every insert and update, such as `updated_at`, make it the table's `replication_key`. If rows are only ever inserted, set `change_history` to `appends`. If rows are also updated and there is no such column, set `change_history` to `changes`. A table with none of these is read in full on every sync. If a table has both a cursor and change history, change history wins.

steps.title: Turn on change history for tables set to changes
steps.text: Run `ALTER TABLE dataset.table SET OPTIONS(enable_change_history=true)` once in BigQuery for that table. It changes no data.

steps.title: Set each table's primary key
steps.text: Add `primary_keys` with the column or columns that identify one row, unless the table already declares a primary key.

steps.title: Send the settings when you configure
steps.text: Through the API or SDK, send the per-table settings as `table_configs` on the same Configure Connector request that selects the tables. The dashboard collects them on the table-selection screen.

examples.intro: One `table_configs` entry per table, for each sync mode:

connect.account: One connector reads one Google Cloud project.

documents.name: Table rows
documents.one_document: One row of a selected table, as long as the table's key is unique. Rows that share a key replace one another.
documents.title: The first non-empty column named `name`, `title`, `subject`, `summary` or `email`. Otherwise the first non-empty column that is not a number, in alphabetical column order, then the first number column. A row with none of these is titled with its table and row key.
documents.text: The title on the first line. Then every non-empty column in alphabetical order, as `Column Name: value`: underscores become spaces and words are capitalised. Lists of values are joined with commas. Nested records are written as compact JSON.
documents.date: The first of `updated_at`, `modified_at`, `last_modified`, `updated`, `created_at`, `created`, `timestamp`, `event_time` and `inserted_at` that holds a TIMESTAMP or epoch-seconds value. A row with none has no date. DATETIME columns carry no time zone and are not used.
documents.files: None. Column values are kept as text only.

attributes.name: Row text
attributes.text: Every non-empty column of the row, written as described above. This is what a query matches.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the row in results. It is also the first line of the row text, so a query matches it.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: The value of the first recognised time column. It is the document date used for recency. A sync cursor with another name does not set it.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The table as `dataset.table`. Limits a query to one table.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The table as `dataset__table`, with two underscores. Another way to limit a query to one table.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's documents.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `bigquery`. Limits a query to BigQuery documents.

attributes.name: table
attributes.text: The table as `dataset.table`, so you can see where a result came from.

attributes.name: row_key
attributes.text: The key the row was matched on. Together with the table, it decides which document a later sync updates.

graph.connections: None. Rows are not linked to each other or to items in other tools, even when a column holds another table's key.
people: None are declared. Each row is grouped under its table.
A column such as `email` or `user_id` is part of the row text only. It does not make the row a person in the graph.
graph.from_text: Everything else. Customers, people, products and references between rows are found only by HydraDB reading the row text.

notes: BigQuery dataset, table, row-level and column-level access controls are not reproduced.
Every column of a selected table becomes searchable text, including sensitive ones. Select tables with that in mind.

sync.first_sync: A table with a cursor column reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. A change-history table starts capturing changes at its first sync, not when you create the connector, and then loads its existing rows in slices of 1,000 per sync. Set `snapshot` to `none` to skip existing rows, or to a number to load at most that many rows, in no particular order. With `none`, changes between creating the connector and its first sync are not recovered.
sync.changes: A cursor table picks up rows whose cursor value moved past the last sync. A `changes` table reads BigQuery's change history, about 11 minutes behind the current time. An `appends` table sees new rows only. A table with neither is read in full on every sync, and rows whose content did not change are skipped.
sync.edits: An edited row updates the same document, as long as its key is unique. In `appends` mode, edits to existing rows are never seen.
sync.deletes: Deleted rows are not removed. A row deleted in BigQuery stays searchable in HydraDB.
notes: BigQuery keeps change history for its time-travel window, 2 to 7 days. If a change-history table is not synced within that window, for example while the connector is paused, the table is skipped with an error on each sync until it is loaded again from the start.

not_synced: Rows deleted in BigQuery: they stay in HydraDB.
Updates to existing rows in tables set to `appends`.
BigQuery dataset, table, row-level and column-level access controls.
Table and column descriptions and other schema details. Only row values are kept.
questions: What does the `sales.orders` table say about order 10432?
Which rows in `crm.accounts` mention Acme Corp?
Which rows in `support.tickets` were updated most recently?
What plan and region are recorded for jane@example.com in `billing.customers`?

good_to_know.title: Large tables need a sync mode.
good_to_know.text: A table with no cursor column and no change history is read in full on every sync, which is expensive on large tables.

good_to_know.title: Change-history rows carry two extra lines.
good_to_know.text: In change-history mode, each row also has `_change_type` and `_change_timestamp` columns, and both appear in the row text.

good_to_know.title: A cursor column does not always set the date.
good_to_know.text: Recency uses only the time column names listed above. A cursor with another name drives sync without setting the document date.

good_to_know.title: Backfill is best effort.
good_to_know.text: Deleting rows while existing rows are still loading can make other rows be missed.
